dailyInsight.headline: Treat cancellation as a separate contract from typed agent output
dailyInsight.insight: PydanticAI has added a cancellation backstop for a durable run whose awaited activity or hook absorbs an external cancellation. Its fresh source and test work make a practical project-scoped call: if an agent can start long-running work, audit whether its completion path can still distinguish a valid result from a cancellation that a lower layer consumed.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The inspected implementation re-checks Python's pending cancellation state at agent-run step and hook boundaries after completed messages have been recorded. The public hardening follow-up says this is a policy signal rather than proof of outside intent, while the Temporal-focused test models an activity that absorbs cancellation and requires the workflow to end cancelled and replay its history.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: Typed dependencies, tool arguments, and structured output can constrain the data an agent exchanges, but they do not establish whether an asynchronous run was interrupted safely. A system that lets cancellation turn into success can schedule follow-on work, show a misleading completion, or run the wrong cleanup path even when every value passing through its schema is valid.

actions.label: Audit one cancellation boundary
actions.instruction: Choose one run that awaits a model stream, tool activity, or event handler. In a non-production test, cancel it while the awaited component catches cancellation and returns normally; verify that the top-level run reports cancellation, records already completed work distinctly, and cannot run downstream success hooks.

receipts.title: Re-assert absorbed external cancellation at run step boundaries (#6496)
receipts.supports: Shows the project added explicit pending-cancellation checks around agent-run advancement and capability-hook boundaries after completed messages have been recorded.

receipts.title: Test the cancellation backstop under real Temporal (#6767)
receipts.supports: Shows a fresh public test design for an activity that absorbs cancellation, a workflow expected to end cancelled, and deterministic history replay.

confidence.basis: The fresh implementation, its public failure description, the explicit hardening caveat, and the Temporal-focused test all describe the same project-scoped cancellation boundary.

dailyInsight.limitation: These are source-level PydanticAI receipts. They do not establish a released package, behavior in every runtime or provider, or that an application has made external side effects reversible.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise this call if a later public change removes the boundary checks, changes the documented policy, or shows that a cancelled run can still reach a normal completion path after an awaited component absorbs cancellation.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for release notes and further runtime tests that extend this cancellation contract beyond the Temporal-focused case, especially around provider streams and external tool effects.
